thread:
Anya Li: quick thought — we should standardize an "incremental rollforward" pattern for model version upgrades. current canary steps feel ad-hoc and it's hard to reason about telemetry delays.
Ben Ortiz: agree. can you sketch what you mean by incremental? percent steps? request-count? time windows?
Anya Li: percent steps + time windows probably simplest for UI. e.g. 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with each step having a duration and safety guards.
Carlos M.: +1 but 0.5% might be too small for low-traffic customers — noisy telemetry. we should allow fallback to absolute request count threshold too.
Dana Patel: for telemetry guards we should use both short-window signal (1m p95 spikes, 5xx rate) and a slightly longer confirm window (5m) before auto-abort. immediate rollback for catastrophic 5xx surge.
Eve K.: UX question: how much control do we expose in Console? free-form JSON/YAML vs a set of templates? I'd prefer templates + an "advanced" editor.
Anya Li: templates for most users, advanced for power users. templates could be "Safe Ramp", "Fast Ramp", "Experiment Split".
Ben Ortiz: also need routing policy semantics: do we route by percent of requests (random sampling) or by user bucket (sticky routing for stateful features)? both. with sticky we need hashing key and a way to drain.
Carlos M.: hashing key + stable bucketing is necessary for A/B tests; for pure model quality rollouts we can do random sampling. UI should warn when sticky bucketing + model variant has KV-cache incompatibilities.
Dana Patel: guard thresholds proposal: - abort if 5xx rate > 0.5% absolute increase vs baseline AND the absolute 5xx rate > 0.2% over 1m window; - abort if p95 latency increases by >30% vs baseline for 2 consecutive 1m buckets.
Eve K.: sounds reasonable. for console alerts, show baseline numbers and % delta inline. also add a "preview estimated tokens" gauge so customers see cost impact during rollouts.
Anya Li: yes. we also need to handle telemetry lag: metrics backend has ~90s to 3m delay depending on aggregation. so step durations should be at least 5m by default, with an option for shorter experimental runs.
Ben Ortiz: default durations: 10m per step? that gives 2*aggregation windows and a little slack. for fast ramp template we can do 3m steps but require manual approval beyond 25%.
Carlos M.: agree. also need a max allowed user override to force-stop rollouts. and RBAC: who can approve emergency continue/abort?
Dana Patel: ops team said they want an automatic mute for noisy metric blips — a rate-limited alerting policy. but rollback should never be rate-limited.
deploy-bot: Deployment scheduled: incremental-rollforward v2.3 -> v2.4; steps: [0.5%, 2%, 10%, 50%, 100%]; step_duration=10m; guards=enabled.
Anya Li: draft DSL for rollout config (for API & Console to share):
```yaml
rollout:
  strategy: incremental
  steps:
    - percent: 0.5
      duration: 10m
    - percent: 2
      duration: 10m
    - percent: 10
      duration: 10m
    - percent: 50
      duration: 15m
    - percent: 100
      duration: 0m
  guards:
    - name: p95_latency
      compare_to: baseline
      window: 1m
      consecutive_buckets: 2
      threshold_percent_increase: 30
    - name: five_xx_rate
      compare_to: baseline
      window: 1m
      threshold_absolute: 0.2
      relative_increase: 0.5
  hashing_key: customer_id # optional, for sticky routing
  fallback_policy: failover_to_previous_model
```
Ben Ortiz: that looks good. two notes: 1) support min_request_count per step: sometimes 0.5% yields <100 requests. 2) make durations configurable per-step in console.
Carlos M.: add 'smoothing' for sudden spikes — e.g. require that the 1m window signal is confirmed by a moving-average over 5m before aborting beyond some thresholds.
Dana Patel: prefer abbreviating complexity in templates and exposing advanced knobs in the API. make sure audit log captures every auto-abort decision (metrics + snapshot) for postmortem.
Eve K.: Console UX: show step timeline, estimated user list impacted (approx), telemetry preview, and a single big red "Abort rollout" button plus a less prominent "Pause" and "Continue". also show reason snippets when rollout auto-aborts.
Anya Li: question for platform infra — can we efficiently compute baselines per-customer at scale? We need baseline windows for latencies and error rates per route/model combo.
Ben Ortiz: infra note: we can approximate baselines with weighted exponential moving averages to keep storage small. but per-customer baselines are heavier. maybe per-tenant baseline + quick warm-up for new tenants.
Carlos M.: request that telemetry include sample traces for flagged requests (sanitized) so SREs can debug model-induced regressions. need privacy considerations.
Dana Patel: add guard for safety regressions too: content-safety rate increase should be monitored as a separate signal (if enabled).
Anya Li: next steps: 1) finalize DSL fields (Ben/Carlos) 2) Console mockups (Eve) 3) infra feasibility + cost estimates (Ben/Dana) 4) ship templates and secret opt-in for early customers.
Eve K.: I'll put a quick mock in Figma and drop link here tomorrow. :+1:
Ben Ortiz: I'll prototype API shape and add min_request_count & smoothing flags.
Carlos M.: I'll draft metric query patterns for the guards and list required telemetry fields.
Dana Patel: I'll sync with SRE about alerting + RBAC for abort approvals.
Anya Li: awesome. thanks team. tagging follow-ups for next week's eng-platform sync. :rocket:
deploy-bot: Note: automated canary monitoring will post summary to #deployments every step.
